extracted.intended_audience: aspiring memoirists and creative nonfiction writers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and philosophical guidance for writing and revising personal memoirs, including voice, truth, craft, psychological readiness, and everyday practices that improve memoir work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision is the source of quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful writing is rooted in extensive revision rather than initial drafts; quality comes from revision and radical edits are crucial to enduring works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renowned authors (Yeats, Eliot) demonstrate radical editing; 'Every writer I know who’s worth a damn spends way more time "losing" than "winning"' and 'Revision is the secret to their troubles—and yours.' Aim to revise repeatedly; expect published pages to look very different from first drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing is often painful and demanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing is frequently a painful process, involving self-interrogation and slow, challenging progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that development moves from defensiveness to self-doubt; balance the generative and editorial selves; be prepared for emotional difficulty when confronting craft and truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read widely and historically to raise standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad reading background, especially in literary history, raises a writer’s standards and deepens understanding of writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delving into past texts gives a more stable sense of quality than following contemporary trends and enriches voice and context; keep a commonplace book and reading journal to copy and reflect on exemplary passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance generative and editorial selves
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers have a generative self (produces material) and an editorial self (refines and interrogates material); both are necessary and must be balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow generative enthusiasm to create drafts, then employ the editorial self to ask hard questions about clarity, emotional impact, and reader experience; alternate modes rather than conflating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate a critical self but avoid despair
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing a critical eye is vital, but rising standards can create feelings of inadequacy when skills lag taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the normal transition from defensiveness to self-doubt; use curiosity in revision to turn perceived mistakes into opportunities rather than sinking into paralysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain humility and high standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for standards that exceed your current abilities; ground ambition in humility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book urges foundations of humility for grand creative aims: 'The higher your structure is to be, the deeper must be its foundation.' Let a sense of quality push revisions rather than ego.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace curiosity during revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach revision with curiosity so that mistakes become opportunities for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than protecting ego, interrogate the work: ask what’s unclear or what emotional beat isn’t landing; seek peer feedback (workshops) to gain perspectives beyond self-critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use collaboration/peer workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration with others can provide valuable insights that self-critique misses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share drafts in workshops to reveal blind spots and alternative readings; peers can point out where voice, stakes, or clarity falter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and honesty are central (the truth contract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoir relies on a contract of truth between writer and reader; authenticity matters and fabrication undermines trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While memory is fallible and some shaping is expected, any embellishment or invention should be handled transparently; small falsehoods can taint the whole work ('a small amount might seem harmless ... but it fundamentally taints the whole experience').

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge subjectivity and fallibility of memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory is mutable and subjective; memoirists should acknowledge this fallibility rather than falsely claiming perfect accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers can bend facts but should disclose their standards of 'truthiness'; consult others when necessary and be candid with readers about uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not write memoir for self-serving reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid writing a memoir primarily for revenge, therapy, or other self-serving motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr advises assessing psychological readiness; if writing is driven by vengeance or unresolved trauma, wait until balanced perspective is possible. Distance (waiting years) often yields more objective and useful insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological readiness and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider your psychological state before undertaking memoir; waiting years after events can allow for insight and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mindfulness and pacing; put drafts aside (e.g., for a week) to gain perspective before revising; avoid writing immediately out of raw emotion unless you can maintain necessary distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set emotional stakes early
rubrics_metrics.description: The book’s thrust or through line should be evident early—emotional stakes must be set so readers understand what's at risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with the split self or inner conflict that drives the narrative; small anecdotes can cumulatively reveal the larger Story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice is foundational
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice is the primary determinant of a memoir’s success; it is the delivery system for experience and must sound authentic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should sound like the author in person; it must allow a range of tones (avoid too wiseass or too pathetic extremes); consistency in diction and syntax helps voice feel true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator must change over time
rubrics_metrics.description: A memoir should demonstrate growth or change in the narrator—static narrators make for weak books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify an 'inner enemy' or structuring problem that propels the narrator’s arc; ensure the narrator evolves across the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bitter, vengeful, or self-pitying tones
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless there's a compelling political motive, bitter or vengeful memoirs tire readers; avoid repetitive victim narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware 'butt-whipping' memoirs that chronicle endless suffering without insight; aim for nuance, hope, wisdom, or psychological endurance rather than pure grievance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render scenes in carnal, sensory detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Use vivid sensory details ('carnal terms') to make scenes believable and visceral; physical clarity helps readers 'believe' the rendered experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjure smells, sounds, textures, and tastes; specific concrete images build trust in memory and enrich the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good prose aims for transparency ('windowpane')
rubrics_metrics.description: Good prose should be clear and unobtrusive—like a windowpane—letting the scene and emotion show without distracting mannerisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gimmicky style that draws attention away from truth; use humor or a judicious adult voice to guide readers through dark material when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confess flaws and darker traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Confession of one's own flaws and darker impulses adds depth and authenticity to memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers respond to vulnerability; resisting the urge to pose or seem palatable often yields stronger, truer voice and material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical daily/technical habits to improve craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete practices—keep a commonplace book, write reviews or criticism, keep a reading journal, write longhand index cards or letters—sharpen judgment and craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy beloved poems/prose to learn choices; writing criticism disciplines evidence-based opinion; memorize poems to learn economy; longhand prompts different mental processing useful for drafting and character work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put drafts aside and re-evaluate with distance
rubrics_metrics.description: After drafting, set work aside for a while before revising to gain perspective on missing material, biases, and self-consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suggested pause is a week before revisiting, then ask how others might view events and what else needs to be said.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support claims with evidence and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Back up opinions and narrative claims with concrete evidence and specifics rather than vague generalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing reviews/criticism teaches how to find and marshal evidence; details (price, object, sensory fragments) anchor memory and lend credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use humor and tonal variation judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor and shifts in tone can help readers traverse dark places and make the voice more engaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone may vary, but keep voice consistent; use humor to balance pathos without undercutting emotional stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth can evolve—revisit and revise over time
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer’s understanding of events and truth can change; revisiting work can reveal new angles and deeper truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that memoirs may be revised as perspective changes, but maintain transparency to readers about the subjective nature of recollection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overusing yourself as source material (self-quotation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on your own previously published lines or repeatedly quoting yourself displays lack of creativity or humility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with broader literary influences instead of recycling your own material; cultivate humility in referencing.
